As you asked the question I thought of an example a friend of mine told me a few weeks ago, where he found it strange when he found two people of the same rank and described the difficulties they were having getting on with that, but in response to your question is it possible, yes, it is happening right now in the UK.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: With respect to this situation where we had apparently Colonel Blaskic and Colonel Kraljevic, did you learn what their relationship was in fact in the HVO chain of command as a result of your study or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner of this ratification or order, we see the titles and I assume -- may I enquire, Mr. President, does the court have this? If not we can put it on the ELMO. This is the attachment to appendix --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The attachment to appendix I. It is the order signed by Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The certificate? Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you see the title at the upper left-hand corner, "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna, Department for Defence, Unit Vitezovi, Vitez"; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know where the Department for Defence was located within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it in Vitez, or was it somewhere else or do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Without being an expert, I think the Department for Defence -- I infer from that address group that we are simply talking about the HVO, as opposed to as you or I would have the Department for Defence as a separate entity in Washington or London.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you would expect to see the same title on other orders issued, for example, by Colonel Blaskic or brigade commanders within the central operative zone of the HVO, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask you, the seal on the original version of this order has not been translated on the English copy, I do not know, Mr. President, if it is translated on the French, but you said you had developed some facility in the language during your duties in the former Yugoslavia. Can you help us, if you are comfortable doing it, translate the seal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think if you look closely, you will see that the words on the seal are exactly the same as the words on the address group, it is fairly clear in the version that I have. I am not sure how many times yours has been copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask my colleague whose pronunciation is much better than mine, let me ask him to lead the phrases in the seal, starting with the uppermost outer ring, progressing down to the middle and then the bottom rings, going from inside to the outer portion of the circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the upper circle, "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina". Below that, "Croatian Community" and then the following line, "Herceg-Bosna". In the bottom part, it is first written down" Vitez, then the "Unit PN", which means for special activities, and then -- special purpose -- and in the end, "the Department for Defence".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is the same words as the address group.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So that confirms, if you heard the translation that the booth was kind enough to give us, that confirms that the seal replicates the various titles of the upper left-hand portion of this order or certificate, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: May I ask that Exhibit D74 be placed before the witness?. This, I think, Mr. President, we will need to put on the ELMO. By way of background, this is a joint order and I would like the seal to be put on the ELMO, this is on the back of the document. This is a joint order of the HVO and the BiH army, also countersigned by Jeremy Fleming, the chairman of the Joint Commission, ECMM, and I would like to direct your attention, and perhaps we could zoom in on the two seals. Thank you. Again, let me ask my colleague to read in the same fashion the HVO seal, that is the written elements of that seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, where the signature of Colonel Blaskic is, there is a seal and in the first line it says, "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina"; below that, "Croatian Community", third line, "Herceg-Bosna". The bottom part has number 1, first line "Travnik", below "Travnik" it is written "Operational Zone Central Bosnia", and below that, "Department for Defence".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So can we conclude that the seal on the Kraljevic order differs from the seal on Exhibit D74 in that D74 refers to the Operative Zone Central Bosnia, while the seal on page I1-1 of Exhibit 242 refers to the special purposes unit, Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you discuss with Commander Dugalic in any more detail to whom this Vitezovi unit and Colonel Kraljevic answered, who their commander was in a chain of command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me return to the substance and text of the Dugalic interview. Is it fair to say that Mr. Dugalic attempted to persuade you that he had proof that the HVO had attacked Ahmici on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I said earlier, he claimed that he had two HVO prisoners who had been present at Ahmici and as I said earlier, as you can imagine I was quite keen to meet these two chaps and unfortunately by the time that I was able to push him on the point, it seemed that they had been released. He showed me uniform patches, shoulder titles or something which he claimed proved the point and I said, "thanks very much, but you could have got these from anywhere."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did he show you the two HVO patches before he had even made the claim to you that he had two HVO soldiers in custody, who had been apprehended in the course of the conflict in Ahmici in mid April 1993? I will refer you to your comment on page 2 of your meeting narrative.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am fairly sure that he talked about the people first, then he produced what he was trying to suggest was evidence and I said, this was one of the occasions that I was actually quite forceful with somebody who in my view was giving me something which was complete rubbish, and I said, "thank you very much, this proves nothing, you could have got these from anywhere. Let me see the people", and, of course, I could not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask you if your comment is accurate or not. Your comment on this page of the report says: "After some persuasion Dugalic first said that they knew that the HVO had been there because they had badges taken from them. He produced HVO and MUP badges, which I rejected because they could have come from anywhere. Then he said that they had captured two HVO. I am not sure whether this was a complex deception, because he never actually let me see the men." Does that refresh your recollection as to whether he first offered these patches and only you rejected that as proof? Did he mention or assert that he had two prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because this was typed so soon after the actual meeting, then I imagine that yes, that is probably the order in which it happened. At this point, looking back on it, I cannot remember which was produced first.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You did express interest on 9th May 1993, did you not, in seeing the men, but he told you that you could not see them at that time, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: On 11th May, two days later, you went back and saw Commander Dugalic a second time, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That meeting is memorialised in appendix Q of your report. At that meeting, did you again press your request to see these two alleged HVO prisoners arrested in the act, if you will, in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because again as you can imagine it struck me as being very important if one could actually get to see people who had been there to meet them and ask them for their view as to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: He told you he had set them free in an exchange, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that they had been set free, not that he had set them free, but the essence was that they had gone so I could not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: At this same period of time, various authorities, including military authorities in Zenica, were pressing a demand for some more information about what exactly had occurred in Ahmici, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you find it credible that if there had been two men captured in Ahmici in the course of that conflict, suspected of participating in the massacre, that they would have been released as part of some exchange in the Lasva Valley; did you find that credible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could imagine how that could have happened. As you can see from the comment that I made in the previous meeting, because of the circumstances, I was not sure whether he ever actually had any people at all and I was not sure whether he was simply trying to lead me up the garden path by saying, "yes, we have some people who were there" or not, so particularly with this level of distance from the events, I have no idea whether those two people actually existed. He did give me the names of people he said had been there, I am not sure whether they exist, whether one would be able to track them down to find out. All I can do at this stage is offer you the notes that I wrote and my memory as best it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So I take it in the end you were left not knowing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I suppose that there are quite a number of questions that you have to ask, maybe it would be a good moment for a break now. In that case, we will have a break and we will start again at 4.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you may continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I expect to conclude in perhaps 15 minutes time, with the court's permission. Let me direct your attention to your interview with Colonel Blaskic. Other than Mr. Friis-Pedersen and the interpreters, was anyone else present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which annex are you referring to please, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Annex G, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: At any point in the interview, did Colonel Blaskic express any ethnic animosity towards any ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think that he was saying to me that he felt that people ought to be able to live together. I am not sure if what he was saying and what was happening were consistent, but that is what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is what he was saying he wanted or wished would happen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did he make any comments suggesting that populations needed to be moved or that population movement was part of a solution that he saw? I can tell you there is nothing in your statement to that effect. Is there anything else you recall to that effect from your interview with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he certainly said that there was a need to withdraw forces or separate forces. I am not sure if he would have gone as far thereafter to say we then need to have the same population displacement as we had very clearly from the mayor of Vitez. The mayor was extremely explicit. Colonel Blaskic was not explicit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Colonel Blaskic, he was not even implicit, was he? He said Croats and Muslims needed to live together in peace and that there needed to be a separation of military forces; that is what he said, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In that regard, I take it his comments on this subject were different from those of Mr. Santic and/or Mr. Skopljak, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Markedly different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think I even have a note to the effect that I commented on the fact that what he was saying seemed to be slightly out of step with what I had just heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: He responded, did he not, that there was a difference between his view, the view of the military in Vitez, and the politicians, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You asked him to mark a map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you have that map with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, in fact I have the original copy and it is here, I can put it on the machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If you would and if we could activate the ELMO? Mr. President, I have spoken to Mr. Harmon and I think we can agree that we would ask that a colour photograph of this map be taken so that it can be used as the map in the exhibit and we need not rely on a handmade replica of the map to constitute the map that is the part of Exhibit 242. Again, if we could call up the map on the ELMO, please? Thank you. Can you tell us as specifically as you can what is you asked Colonel Blaskic to do with respect to this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have put the map on the table with the pens and asked him to illustrate his explanation of what was going on on the map. I cannot remember whether he actually drew a second map which had arrows indicating the various lines of attack. He may have done, but I am not sure. Certainly what is represented on this map was his understanding of the ethnic makeup of the villages around Vitez. If I move the map down briefly so one can see the key which I have added, you can see that they are colour coded, orange for mainly Croatian villages or centres of population, green for mainly Muslim villages or centres of population and pink for mixed areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If you could move the map up now to the middle and if we could move in slightly please on the villages that have been marked in colour. Thank you. If you look at this map, it is difficult to see on the ELMO, but are there two villages which are not yellow, they are not pink and they are not green, they are some other colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as you can see I have indicated here on the map the villages of Ahmici and Nadioci are coloured in yellow and blue. This is the only marking on the map which was made subsequent to my meeting with Colonel Blaskic. I highlighted those two villages to make the point that he had omitted to put any colour on them during our meeting and there is a note to that effect in the text of the report, as you will have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Other than those two villages, the coloured markings on the map were made by him, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the interview, he referred to a build-up of BiH army forces in Travnik in the week or so prior to and including April 15th 1993, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that consistent with other information you received in the course of your study?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Directing your attention down that first page, he also described for you the location of certain BiH army brigades. Specifically in Zenica, there were three BiH army brigades, as well as the 7th Muslim brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And there was a battalion of the 305th BiH army Brigade in Busovaca, he also told you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were those facts consistent with what you learned from other sources in the course of your study?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not actually cross-reference with anybody else to find out what brigade or battalion numbers were and precisely what troop deployments were, so the fact that there were troops in those places or near those places is not inconsistent, but in terms of those particular units as numbered by him, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You did not check the brigade numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to the third paragraph from the end, beginning with the phrase, "on 23rd January, the Busovaca to Kiseljak road was cut." Do you find that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The next sentence is: "Busovaca was occupied and ethnically cleansed." When he made that statement to you, first of all, did you understand him to be referring to the fact that the road from Busovaca to Kiseljak was cut and taken by the BiH army between Kacuni and Bilalovac on or about 23rd January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not be as precise as you have been in terms of the villages where it was cut, but I understood it was cut between the two main centres of Busovaca and Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you also understand him to be saying that that portion of the Busovaca municipality that had been taken and occupied by the BiH army in the course of the January 1993 conflict, that that territory had been ethnically cleansed of Croats; is that what you understood him to be telling you in that paragraph, or did you have an understanding as to what he was telling you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Given the context and my understanding of what was happening in Busovaca, the town itself, either there was a misinterpretation or he must have been referring to the territory which was taken by the ABiH, because I do not think that he would have been telling me that the HVO had ethnically cleansed Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you did understand at the time that he was referring to ethnic cleansing by the BiH army forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure at the time that I reached a conclusion. Sitting here, logically it has -- I think it has to be either one of those two conclusions, that there was a misinterpretation at the time, a mis-translation, so that I wrote down something other than what he said, or that he was referring to territory which the ABiH had ethnically cleansed, because I assume that he was not saying that the HVO had ethnically cleansed Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you to return to your notes and write-up of the interview of Commander Dugalic, which is appendix I. You have told us, and this is towards the latter part of your statement, that you discussed with Commander Dugalic, the intelligence officer or commander attached to the III Corps, the issue of the truck bomb which exploded in Stari Vitez on or about April 18th 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Dugalic asserted to you that while Kraljevic had carried out the attack, Blaskic, he asserted, had ordered it, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You had previously met with General Halilovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Had he made that assertion to you, that Blaskic had ordered the truck bomb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that subject had not come up at all in the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You had previously met with Hadzihasanovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did he assert to you in your meeting with him that Blaskic had ordered the truck bomb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did Commander Dugalic, the intelligence officer attached to III Corps, did he provide any source for this allegation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you ask him for his source, or a source?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as with everything else, I was simply taking a note of what people were telling me without challenging them in most cases for exactly what they were saying, so I was not coming back to them and saying, "this is preposterous, please tell me more", or indeed "how do you know?", with the exception of him claiming to have two Croatian soldiers, which I thought was particularly interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So to summarise, in your interview you did not cross-examine or challenge him at all with respect to his source or basis of knowledge for this allegation, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Have you been told whether the Office of the Prosecutor or their investigators have sought to interview Commander Dugalic to confirm or deny or discover any basis, whether there is any basis for this allegation; have you been told anything pertaining to that subject?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the course of the rest of your study, did you make any efforts to try and confirm, deny, corroborate or whatever this allegation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the course of your study, did you obtain any evidence from any other source tending to support this allegation, the allegation that Colonel Blaskic ordered a truck bomb, that a truck bomb be deployed and detonated within Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So this allegation is the only item of information that you collected in the course of your nine day study on this subject pertaining to Colonel Blaskic, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: To this day, have you heard any evidence from any source whatsoever that would tend to support or corroborate that allegation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since then, I have taken absolutely no interest in following it up, so no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I take it at the end of your interviews with Commander Dugalic you were not in a position to evaluate the worth, credibility or lack thereof of that item of information he had given you, his allegation that Colonel Blaskic ordered a truck bomb, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I have said earlier on, in each case, all I was attempting to do was write down what people wanted to tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Now let me direct your attention to your interview with the Imam of Busovaca, which is appendix K. He told you, I take it, that he had had certain contacts with Zoran Maric who was an HVO civilian authority; was that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we look at the fourth paragraph, I have the description I was given which is that he was with the president of Busovaca, currently Zoran Maric, of HVO, so I am not clear whether the president of HVO would be a civilian or a military person, HVO normally being a military entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will refrain from commenting and simply accept your answer. Is it correct to say that the Imam told you in your interview that Zoran Maric had promised protection to the Muslim community, that is in paragraph 5, and then on the second page that: "Maric really wants to help but thinks that he cannot." Did the Imam say those things to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did he say, and this is in the third paragraph from the bottom on the first page, that specifically refugees, Croat refugees were coming to Busovaca and were threatening Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I am looking at the third paragraph from the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Third paragraph from the end of the first page, the bottom line of the third paragraph from the end on page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Two paragraphs above that, he provides a little detail, did he not, when he recited and described how a family made homeless comes into town, Croat houses having been burned in outlying villages in the Busovaca municipality and then that family takes over a Muslim house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the next page, you commented on the statement on this page that, "Kordic seems to be the man calling the shots", again repeating that idiomatic expression. Now I want to ask you again, in light of your explanation of when you used a comment and the word "comment" to indicate your own insights and material versus the text of these statements which you have indicated represents what the witnesses said, I want to ask you again, this statement regarding Mr. Kordic, is that something that the Imam said, or is it your own side comment, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is certainly written in my notes, so it is a note made at the time and we could look at it if you want to and see how it fits into the flow of the conversation. It was a note written at the time of the meeting. Because of where it fits into the flow of the conversation where he was showing me his pass and we were having -- I was making a note of who had signed the pass, I am not sure whether we had clearly -- I had broken from writing detailed notes and was looking at this thing. Given the language which is used, I cannot imagine that is actually the language which the Imam would have used, so I think that is my picking up the flow of my notes again by saying what I said. At this point, looking back, I think it is probably my summary of the situation that I was hearing as opposed to my writing town precisely what the Imam had said. Four and a half years on it is quite difficult to remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you say that in part because you believe that the idiomatic expression "calling the shots" does not exist in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea whether it exists or not. I am sure they have something similar. It may be that the interpreter had taken a Bosnian idiom and translated it as "calling the shots". At this stage, I just do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you check your notes to see whether they reflect that this was a comment by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can do it again now if you would like me to, but I did check my notes and it is written into the flow of the notes as I was taking them, which suggests that it was either me picking up the flow of the conversation, or it was something which was actually said. We can go round this as many times as we like, but I am not sure we can add much clarity to it, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I do not want to belabour it. Turning your attention to your next interview with the chief of police in Busovaca, appendix L, I take it he told you that the suspects in this rape case would have to be tried in the only court that existed at the time, which was in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I explained earlier, I was attempting to establish what the judicial process was and was asking them questions about what they would do with a suspect if they arrested them, where would they try them, would they be in prison, where would they be in prison, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Now let me direct your attention to your overall conclusions which are set forth on pages 1 and 2 of your report. You wrote in paragraph 5 that: "The Muslim reaction from Zenica", to the events of April 16th, "was to attack the key road junctions east of Vitez and north of Busovaca." When you wrote that, are you referring to two different pieces of road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think what I am referring to is what is known as the Busovaca T junction, so the road from Zenica to Vitez which then has a T junction and goes south to Busovaca, and I think they were attempting to cut off the road at that point, either on both sides of the T junction or at the T junction itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I ask because you used the word junctions, plural, in your report. Is it your testimony now you are referring to one junction or more than one junction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is one junction. At this point I cannot remember exactly what I was thinking, or exactly what the tactical situation had been as it was described, but what they were fundamentally trying to do was cut the road, thus isolating Busovaca and Vitez, and I am quite clear about that as the intention of what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you mean isolating Vitez and Busovaca from Zenica, or isolating Vitez and Busovaca from each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From each other. At that point it was possible to move from one to the other along the road and my understanding of what the ABiH were trying to do was to cut that communications link, thus having two pockets as opposed to one pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So the Vitez-Busovaca pocket had already been cut off from the Kiseljak enclave, correct? It was cut off in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that road had been reopened, actually. I cannot remember precisely. When I left, I drove down the road -- I cannot remember who was in control of the central part of it. I think actually it was under Croatian control all the way along, but I may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The record is clear on that point and I do not need to debate it with you. With respect to the Vitez-Busovaca spinal road, are you saying that the Muslim strategy was, in their attack, was to cut the spinal road between Vitez and Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding of what they were trying to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that an obvious military strategy, a strategy of -- a well thought out military strategy, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure it is for me to comment on high level military strategy. If what they were attempting to do was to defeat the Croatian army, then by dividing the territory controlled by the Croats into small chunks, that would seem to make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And indeed, if you cut the spinal road between Vitez and Busovaca, would you agree that the HVO would no longer be able to marshall troops at any point in a defensive position by running those troops back and forth, up and down the spinal road in order to concentrate them at a point of defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if that is what they were doing by moving troops from one end of the pocket to the other, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said there was a co-ordinated attack on 16th April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that at about 5.30 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is fair to say that attacks -- conflict broke out, I would certainly say that conflict broke out early in the morning, 5.30, 6.30, the reports were different in different places, but the quality of the information differed depending on where there were international observers, but early on the morning of the 16th, fighting broke out in a number of places.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Although not in all the villages of the area, correct? In Gacice, there was no open conflict for several days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you able to determine what HVO units participated in the conflict at any certain geographic point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you able to determine what orders were given at different levels of the HVO with respect to military actions on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you able to determine what reports during the course of that conflict were given up, whatever chains of command existed within the HVO concerning that conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were those issues beyond the scope of your study?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite clearly I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you state again the purpose of your study?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I was trying to do was to meet with people in a balanced way on both sides, with both parties, with the political, the military and the religious leaders, to find out from them what their view of what had happened was, to cross-reference that with what the international community, UNPROFOR and ECMM specifically, thought had happened and as a result of this process of meeting people and hearing what they said had happened, to attempt to draw some conclusions. Given the situation at the time and the length of time that I had been given to be there, and the fact that this was an attempt to get an overview as opposed to a very detailed and precise investigation, I did not feel that it was appropriate even to ask for things like the orders that had been given or the reports that were being made by the parties. Obviously I was seeing the reports that we were making ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you circulate your report and solicit comments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you circulate it to the army of BH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If I could be assisted in providing the witness and counsel with an exhibit? If a copy could be given to the witness, and there are copies for counsel and the court as well. I have provided you with the cover page of your report which is not a part of Exhibit 242 and my question is simple. Under, "distribution external", the third party is listed as "HQ BH COMD". Can you tell us who that refers to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I think you would find would be the UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak. There is certainly no intention to pass it to the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Very well. In a similar vein I take it it was not given to Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Nor was it given to anyone else in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Mr. Harmon, you have perhaps some complementary questions within the framework of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I have a few points of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before that, I would like to ask Mr. Hayman whether he wants this to be admitted into evidence, the cover page of Mr. McLeod's report. I suppose you do? It needs to be identified by the witness, because it is the cover page of his own report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, we would ask that it be admitted, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. What number is it going to have, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. It is your turn, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. McLeod, I would like to turn your attention to annex E, which is your meeting with Father Bozo of Cajdras. You were asked a number of questions in respect of your meeting with Father Bozo and in fact testified that Father Bozo and then Father Stjepan had informed you that a number of houses belonging to Bosnian Croats had been burned, damaged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me also reference you to the last page and your comment, which is found on E-3. Father Bozo also gave you a copy of a letter, did he not, to III Corps in Zenica in which he stated that the situation had stabilised, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you explain what he meant by that, what he said to you in respect of that situation being stabilised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you can see by looking at the appendix 1, which is the translation of the letter which he gave me, which is also attached, he started off by saying that, "we are glad that some less" -- the English is not particularly precise, I am not sure the original is particularly precise: "We are glad some less good people have stopped with burning and mining of houses. The last number is: 15 burned houses and 4 stables and 2 mined houses. "We thank God and good people for no further killings, and our gratitude we direct to the above-mentioned titles", who are the ABiH. So what he was saying was that the situation has been stabilised by the intervention of the ABiH and the police. He then went on to list in detail what had already happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let me focus your attention to your interview with Ramiz Dugalic which is found at annex I. Specifically, Mr. McLeod, I am directing your attention to the second page of the English translation, which focuses on Darko Kraljevic who was a colonel of one of the HVO formations, specifically the legal formation doing the dirty jobs for the HVO; do you see that particular paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In respect of your conversations with Ramiz Dugalic, he then gave you a ratification which we have had considerable testimony about, and it is signed by order of Colonel Darko Kraljevic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the address block on the upper left-hand corner of that document, it indicates from which unit this order emanated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The unit is indicated as the Unit Vitezovi, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would like to have, with the assistance of the usher, I would like to have D42 and D42A placed on the ELMO -- if we could have all three orders given on the usher, Mr. Registrar. Defence Exhibit D42A, D77 and D43A. Now if we could have placed, Mr. Usher, Defence Exhibit 42A on the ELMO, can we focus in please on the right-hand side, upper right-hand side, the address block? That is fine, thank you. First of all, you were asked a number of questions about the chain of command between Colonel Blaskic and Darko Kraljevic, do you remember those questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Referring to Defence Exhibit 42A, does this appear to you to be an order signed by Colonel Blaskic? You have to turn it over.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is signed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you turn that over, please, Mr. McLeod? Do you see to whom the orders were issued? Do you see "Vitezovi special task force" in that particular list of units to which this order was issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is clearly for the attention of the brigades and also the Vitezovi special task force.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the date of this order, sir? 17th March 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if I could have Defence Exhibit 77 placed on the ELMO, does this also, Mr. McLeod, appear to you to be an order issued by Tihomir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, referencing the units to which this order was issued, do you see in there any reference to the Vitezovi special task force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is listed down there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The date of this order is 21st April 1993, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Lastly, let me refer you to Defence Exhibit 43A, if that could be placed on the ELMO please. This order is in French, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is not a defect, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, it is a virtue. I was thinking of the witness, Mr. President. Can you see that particular order, does that appear to be an order that is issued by -- purportedly issued by Tihomir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, so we have the signature block here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if we could go to the front page of that and place that on the ELMO as well. Do you see whether that order was issued to the Vitezovi special task force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, again we can see it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Considering those three particular orders that you have just seen, in your opinion as a military man, under whose chain of command were the Vitezovi special task force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If these are genuine, they quite clearly seem to state that Colonel Blaskic was giving orders to that unit, amongst others.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The unit that was -- the unit of Colonel Darko Kraljevic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I turn now to Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You mentioned that on 16th April, Croatian forces, I am just summing up what you said several times, Croatian forces attacked Muslim positions in the Lasva Valley. Among other things, they arrested prominent Muslims, civilians were killed, houses were razed to the ground. Was this required by any military necessity or was it provoked in such a way that it had to be done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see no -- depending on precisely what the objectives of the Croatian army were, I can see no reason, unless they particularly wanted to drive out the Muslim population and terrorise them, why they needed to do certainly some of the things which they were doing. If their objective was a military offence, I can see no particular reason why they would need to raze a village to the ground as they did at Ahmici, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think in your meeting with Santic, he mentioned to you that, "there is no room for Muslims and they had to leave, so that a democracy can be created like the ones you have in Western Europe". You mentioned something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That was on 15th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My meeting with him was on 10th May, I think. He was describing the situation as he saw it and he was expanding on his, what I believe were his political views and his view of how things ought to happen. I understand that he was saying that, "in order to have democracy, in order to implement the Vance plan, we need to be sure that the majority vote will go the way we want to have it"; this is me paraphrasing what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your report at page 1, you mentioned that categorically the Croats, it is something like the third paragraph from below, that the Croats, the last three lines: "They are using extreme methods of terror and genocide to remove the Muslim population and were only prevented from total success by their miscalculation of the Muslim military." Then in the last paragraph you say: "Events throughout the rest of Central Bosnia-Herzegovina and latterly in Mostar appear to follow the same pattern that emerged in the Vitez area. It is hard to believe that in each case the events are the acts of isolated extremists or agents provocateurs working for the Serbs." So you think it was a scheme aiming at, you described categorically, at genocide and the removal of the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the conclusion that I reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That was the conclusion of your assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You mentioned also that General Blaskic gave an order prohibiting any, in a few words, trespassing on the Muslim houses, beating or looting or torching Muslim houses, and this did not stop, this looting and burning and that sort of thing. Was not General Blaskic the official and legitimate commander of the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I certainly understood when I met him that he was the military commander for the operational zone. I have been shown the order, I have no reason to doubt that it is a genuine order but certainly at the time that I was there, I understand that these things were still going on and so the order had either not been implemented or events had deteriorated again since the order had been implemented, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was his authority disputed by the lower commanders in the area, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was it challenged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no reason to suspect that it was and I approached him because I was told by my colleagues in ECMM that he was their interlocutor in the meetings that they were having trying to stabilise the situation, so in their view, he was the military commander, he was presented as such at the meetings they were having with him on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So his orders were supposed to be obeyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if not obeyed, he was supposed to take action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You spoke of the prison under the provision of Aleksovski and you said it was an HVO prison. Was that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a military prison, HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It was a military prison, the Kaonik Prison. Aleksovski told you that he did not select the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, he explained that prisoners were sent to him and that he had no ability to either accept or reject somebody who was delivered to his front door.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And they were civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly the Muslims that I saw appeared to be civilians and some of them described their jobs and they were people who sounded like civilians to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It was under the HVO command, the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You said there were 68 Muslims inside individual cells. How many were in a cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that there were between six and eight people in each of the cells. I cannot remember precisely, but there were quite a lot of them. It was very tight inside the rooms when we went into each room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Very tight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was the MOS? You mentioned that all authorities joint patrols were doing their best to stabilise the situation, except the MOS. You have an idea who they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they were one of the irregular units. I am not sure precisely what MOS stands for. Perhaps somebody could help. I am not sure exactly which unit they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were they a powerful group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can I say "Lieutenant"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been a civilian for five and a half years now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. McLeod, I am referring to that part of your summary of the meeting between you and Mr. Santic, and Mr. Skopljak, and in particular to the sentence which you say that as written here, it does not reflect what you intended to say. It is at F-2. The sentence reads: "There is a problem with some people who come into people's houses, so Blaskic has ordered his forces not to enter Muslims' houses." I take it you were recording there what was said to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In answer to Judge Riad, you said that Colonel Blaskic had the authority to issue orders which you would expect would be carried out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Had Colonel Blaskic already issued orders prohibiting his own forces from entering the houses of Muslims? Would you expect that the speaker would still say to you that "there is a problem" or that "there used to be a problem"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If he had given an order and the order had been carried out, then I think the speaker would have been saying that, "there had been a problem".

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, but then you said you would expect that any orders issued by Colonel Blaskic would be carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would imagine they should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, was it your impression that the speaker was saying to you, one way or another, that Colonel Blaskic had the authority to issue such orders of prohibition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you were reporting your conversation with Mr. Santic and Mr. Skopljak, you ended with a last paragraph at F-4, in which you gave your final comment. In referring to what they had said you stated: "All of this was said with a straight, if slightly smug face. The suggestion that as a result of a Muslim attack there was a chaotic defence of Vitez in which the Muslims were displaced from their villages around Vitez is incredible."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That represented your concluding impression of that interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When reporting your conversation with Colonel Blaskic, it is my recollection that you said you formed the impression that he was being straightforward with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During those parts of the conversation where we were discussing the military situation and he was describing what had happened after 16th April, the description which he gave matched almost exactly the description which I had been given of those events by members of UNPROFOR, so all of those parts of the conversation fitted into place and seemed to make sense. The point at which I had difficulty believing what he was saying was just to do with his description of what had happened on the morning of 16th April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Of the 16th. In other words, your reference to his manners being straightforward related to his depicting of the military situation consequent on the counterattack by the BiH army and the cutting or the attempt to cut the two roads and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Right. Let us then go back to the morning of the 16th where he said he was surprised early in the morning by the sounds which he heard and he woke up and so on and issued orders. He was the officer who commanded the operational zone in the area inclusive of Vitez and Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In Vitez alone, I think if I look at G-1, the Vitez brigade has 300 to 350 professionals, so you state there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what he told me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the rest are reservists.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As a military officer, would you expect that a commanding officer who has 300 to 350 professionals under his immediate control would be surprised to learn that an event of this kind was taking place in Vitez and Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that if as he was suggesting there had been a surprise attack by the ABiH just before first light or at first light that morning then conceivably he would have been taken by surprise. The reason why I eventually draw the conclusion that I have difficulty believing that is that there were a number of events which were taking place at the same time, most notably the arrest of a number of key people in Vitez, and I cannot reconcile in my own logic how a number of 13 or 14 people, prominent Muslims, were being arrested in their own homes first thing in the morning on the 16th in what in my view, based on my experience of Northern Ireland, must have been a co-ordinated operation to pick them up. I simply cannot reconcile that -- and I actually saw some of them in prison, so that happened -- with a chaotic defence in response to a surprise attack. If there had been a surprise attack, I cannot imagine how a large number of people in a co-ordinated manner could have been running around Vitez arresting people. It just does not tie together.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I see. When you refer to a large number of people mounting a co-ordinated attack, you would be speaking about how many people in respect of Stari Vitez and in respect of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure exactly how many people they would have used. If I had been doing -- I probably would have used almost all the troops which he has, on the basis that I would want to have, as a rule of thumb, a multiple of three times more people attacking than were defending.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is normal military wisdom, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the British army, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The words which you wrote down to report the interview which you had with Colonel Blaskic were these: "Later we found" -- I take it there you are reporting him in the first person, at G-1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fourth paragraph from the bottom: "Later we found heavy fighting in Vitez and in the villages round Vitez." Did he say who were engaged in this heavy fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My inference was that it was the ABiH and the HVO who were fighting. What I have written is as I scribbled my note, as my interpreter translated what he was saying, and so he would have said "later in the morning, we found heavy fighting going on and were reacting to it".

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did he actually say that, that the fighting was between the BiH Army and others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that point I am not sure if he was being specific about the units, but I think we would all have assumed that those were the people he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you ask him any questions as to the identity of the forces which were confronting each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I was quite clear and I think he was also quite clear that this was predominantly the ABiH versus HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So to conclude this likely inquiry of mine, when you described him as giving you the impression of being straightforward, you were not referring to the positions which he took with you in respect of the events which occurred on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have only one question, about your report, was it commented upon by the people to whom it was addressed, the people who read it, were there any critics, any comments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only significant comment which we received was from the German delegation who objected to my use of the word "totalitarian". They felt they understood better than others what totalitarian meant. But that was the only comment of any significance within ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But in all the comments that are diplomatic and strategic, you have covered very many fields by your comments, sometimes you had a very global perception of what was going on. So what were the remarks by your bosses, your superiors, those people who sent you in that mission? What were your procedures? Did they think that you maybe made hasty conclusions or that you have properly judged it? How did they assess your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As soon as we had finished producing and disseminating this report, I was immediately involved with the deputy head of the mission and his political advisor writing a briefing based, amongst other things, on this report which was passed to an EU diplomatic mission, who I believe were convening then at a meeting in Mostar where events had also broken down. I think it is safe to say that the conclusions I had reached were then immediately adopted by the causes of ECMM and incorporated into their further reporting up the chain of command above the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is it your impression that the people you spoke to are the political or military high in rank, that you met some people, or there were some people you were not able to meet that you regret not having been able to meet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only person who was missing from the list that I had drawn up at the beginning in consultation with Ambassador Thebault that I would have liked to have met was Dario Kordic, because we had the impression that he was a significant player. I would have met him at the end of my series of meetings, but events and the timetable were against me and so unfortunately I had to leave him out, but between my view and that of Ambassador Thebault, he would have been a useful person to have had a conversation with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My last question: one of the people you talked to, I do not know whether it was Santic or Skopljak or maybe somebody else, somebody said that maybe could the Vance-Owen Plan be implemented, that that could have improved the situation. It was not one of your comments, it was somebody you talked to who said that, but certainly it is in your report. I cannot remember who told you, I think it was Santic, maybe Skopljak, Santic I would say. How do you feel about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Santic who was suggesting that we should -- that they should implement the Vance-Owen Plan immediately for that area of Central Bosnia. I think that the reason why he was advocating that was that the Vance-Owen Plan would have allowed the establishment of military and political structures based on the ethnic composition of the territory, and so I think that he felt that if the ethnic composition of the territory suited him, in other words if it was Croat dominated, then they would be able to, with some legitimacy, establish a military and political structure which reflected that; in other words a military and political structure which was Croat dominated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you conclude from that that in a way the players that you met were pushing in a very strong way, not to say even more, to the implementation of that Vance-Owen Plan? Maybe they applied methods that could anticipate in a way that that was the way of maybe an ethnic cleansing that was almost officialised by the international community, or maybe you did not have that impression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding of the aim of the Vance-Owen Plan was to reflect the original ethnic makeup as opposed to any ethnic makeup which may have been achieved as a result of the war as it raged back and forth across Bosnia. So I think what one had was a partial interpretation of the spirit of the Vance-Owen Plan, which was then being assisted by a little bit of extreme violence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no more questions. My colleagues, no further questions. Your statement has ended, thank you very much for that. Now we are going to adjourn and tomorrow we will resume, this will be the last day of our two week period of the Blaskic trial. So we will resume tomorrow at 10.00.

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
